sources.title: Market Index Data (BSC glossary)
sources.locator: Glossary Term: Market Index Data, main body paragraphs
quotes: reflects the price of wholesale electricity in Great Britain in the short term markets
The Market Price (the volume weighed average Market Index Price) is used to derive the Reverse Price (SBP or SSP)
sources.supports: E-01: the supplied series is a short-term wholesale index used as an imbalance reference price, not a retail or contract price. Also shows the glossary still uses the pre-single-cash-out SBP/SSP wording.
sources.evidence_strength: high (definition itself); interpretation of the CSV as this index is an inference, see R1-C01

sources.title: Imbalance Pricing
sources.locator: Introduction; 'How it relates to you'; 'Market Index Data Volume and Price'; 'System Prices parameters'
quotes: The Imbalance Price is used to settle energy imbalance volumes
However now there is a single price calculation, so SBP will equal SSP in each Settlement Period
Market Index Data (MID) is used in the calculation of the Market Index Price for each Settlement Period
sources.supports: E-01 and E-04: settlement happens on contracted volume with a single cash-out price for deviations; the index is a settlement input, so revenue equals price x energy only when the plan is fully contracted (the perfect-foresight Tier1 case).

sources.title: Energy price cap and standing charges explained
sources.locator: 'How we calculate the price cap' cost component list; 'Who the price cap protects' exclusion list
quotes: buying energy on the open market (wholesale costs)
building and improving the pipes and wires that transport energy (network costs)
have a business energy contract
sources.supports: E-01 and E-03: a retail tariff is wholesale plus network, policy, operating, EBIT, headroom and VAT components, so the wholesale index cannot be used as a purchase or retail price; business contracts are outside the cap, so no public business ceiling exists.
sources.evidence_strength: high for the structure; no numeric business tariff obtained

sources.title: About the Smart Export Guarantee (SEG)
sources.locator: 'Who is the scheme for?'; 'How does the scheme work?'
quotes: anyone with an installation of one of the following technology types up to a capacity of 5MW
SEG tariff rates must always be above zero
sources.supports: E-07 and E-02: the modelled farm (peak 1125 MW) is far outside the 5 MW SEG threshold, so SEG is not an admissible export route; also confirms small-scale export rates are supplier-set and strictly positive.

sources.title: Charging - the charges for using Great Britain's electricity system
sources.locator: Body text, 'There are four main types of charges' and the four charge descriptions
quotes: TNUoS charges recover the costs of installing and maintaining the transmission system and are charged to all suppliers and generators
BSUoS charges recover the costs of the day-to-day operation of the transmission system
sources.supports: E-07: establishes the four charge families (TNUoS, BSUoS, connection, AAHEDC) and that both suppliers and generators pay TNUoS, so a Scottish connection carries a real fixed charge that the brief's simplification omits.

sources.title: Balancing Services Use of System (BSUoS) charges
sources.locator: 'Who does this charge apply to?' list and the CMP308/CMP361 paragraph
quotes: CMP308 defined that BSUoS charges are recovered solely from final demand, and CMP361 introduced an ex-ante fixed BSUoS tariff
sources.supports: E-07: generators (including embedded generators) are marked as not charged, so a BSUoS deduction from export revenue would be wrong under the post-April-2023 regime.

sources.title: Transmission Network Use of System (TNUoS) Charges
sources.locator: 'Who does this charge apply to?' list; 'How am I charged?' paragraph
quotes: Generators are charged according to Transmission Entry Capacity (TEC), while suppliers are charged based on actual demand
Certain embedded generators (<100MW) receive export payments over triad
sources.supports: E-07: TNUoS on generation is a capacity-based (GBP/kW/year), zonal charge, not a per-MWh charge, so it belongs to fixed cost rather than to dispatch; also shows smaller embedded generators can receive payments rather than pay.
sources.evidence_strength: high for the basis; numeric tariff not obtained

sources.title: Balancing Mechanism Unit (BSC glossary)
sources.locator: Glossary Term: Balancing Mechanism Unit, first paragraph
quotes: BM Units are used as units of trade within the Balancing Mechanism
sources.supports: E-06: constraint-related payments arise through Balancing Mechanism participation, so an unregistered constructed farm has no route to them; supports the zero-compensation baseline.
sources.evidence_strength: medium (establishes the participation requirement, not the payment rules)

sources.title: Supplier (BSC glossary)
quotes: means a Party which holds a Supply Licence and is responsible for Exports and/or Imports
sources.supports: E-03: buying electricity for resale requires supply-licence status and registered metering, so an enabled import route carries an eligibility assumption that must be declared.

sources.title: Balancing costs
sources.locator: Body text, 'Balancing costs' categories and 'Balancing Costs in Consumer Bills'
quotes: System actions deal with the physical limits of the energy system
Balancing costs are one of many components making up consumer energy bills
sources.supports: E-06 and E-07: constraint-driven costs are system actions recovered through charges, not a general payment for not generating; also confirms balancing costs are socialised into bills rather than levied per MWh on generators.

sources.title: LCCC homepage - news item 'Baseload Market Reference Price Winter 2026'
quotes: The Baseload Market Reference Price (BMRP) for Winter 2026, which covers October 2026 to March 2027, is GBP 114.50/MWh
sources.supports: E-01: current published GB baseload reference level (GBP 114.50/MWh) is far above the 2020-2026 supplied daily mean (GBP 48.17/MWh), so the historical mean is not a forecast and price-level sensitivity is mandatory.
sources.evidence_strength: medium (announcement snippet; the underlying BMRP methodology was not opened)
sources.note: Quote rendered with 'GBP' in place of the pound sign only; wording otherwise as displayed.

sources.publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Energy Security and Net Zero collection)
sources.title: GOV.UK search results for 'contracts for difference negative pricing' - entry 'Contracts for Difference'
sources.doc_type: government search listing (secondary presentation of a primary collection)
sources.locator: Result list, second entry 'Contracts for Difference' summary line
quotes: A Contract for Difference (CfD) is a private law contract between a low carbon electricity generator and the Low Carbon Contracts Company (LCCC), a government-owned company
sources.supports: E-01 and E-07: a CfD is a bilateral contract, so the supplied merchant index price cannot be read as a CfD strike or reference price, and no CfD payment belongs in the baseline. The negative-pricing provision itself was NOT obtained (see failed retrievals).
sources.evidence_strength: low-medium (search snippet, collection page not opened)

sources.title: SOURCE_MANIFEST.json
sources.locator: entries for daily_generation_by_fuel.csv, daily_generation_total.csv, daily_demand.csv, wind_farm_generation.csv, daily_market_index_price.csv (columns, data_rows, distinct_dates, sha256)
quotes: columns: date, avg_price_gbp_per_mwh, avg_price_gbp_per_mw_day
sources.supports: E-01: documents the column names and row counts but not the index definition, aggregation rule or weighting, which is why the MIP reading is recorded as an inference (R1-C01, R1-C07).
sources.evidence_strength: high as metadata; silent on the points that matter
sources.note: Quote paraphrases the JSON field names without the pound-sign characters.

sources.title: Project_Brief.pdf, page 6 appendix (battery and electrolyser parameters)
sources.doc_type: course brief (authoritative input, read via the page-marked text extract)
quotes: The electrolyser needs about 55.9 kWh of electricity to produce 1 kg of hydrogen
GBP 9.5/kg as a core scenario
sources.supports: Used only for the H2 electricity-equivalent conversion (R1-C34) and the 90 percent round-trip efficiency in the cycling threshold (R1-C19).

sources.title: BASELINE_1103.md, BL-02, BL-04, BL-06, BL-07, BL-09, BL-11
sources.locator: Sections BL-02 (demand as absorption limit), BL-04 (no intraday spreads), BL-06 (q_t = min{G_t,D_t}), BL-07 (purchases disabled), BL-09 (single-counted opportunity cost), BL-11 (retain negative prices)
quotes: Demand is the system's sales/absorption limit, not an extra unpaid company internal load
sources.supports: The baseline choices this pass tests; R1 finds the D_t cap is a convention without a market analogue, and concurs with the closed-market and negative-price provisions.
